standards.seoTitle: Editorial Standards — How Garzoni Writes Its Lessons
standards.seoDescription: How Garzoni writes, sources, reviews and corrects its personal finance lessons and guides, and why none of it is financial advice.
standards.title: Editorial standards
standards.intro: Garzoni teaches personal finance. Money decisions matter, so we hold our lessons and guides to a few simple rules. This page explains who writes them, where the facts come from, how they are kept up to date and what happens when we get something wrong.

who.heading: Who writes our content
who.body: Every lesson and guide on Garzoni is written and edited by Andrei Neagoe, Garzoni's founder.
who.review: Our content is not currently reviewed by an external financial expert. If that changes, the reviewer will be named here and on each page they review.

writing.heading: How we write lessons
writing.clarity: Plain language. Jargon is explained the first time it appears, and each lesson focuses on one idea you can use.
writing.context: UK context. New and updated lessons use UK figures, rules and examples unless the page says otherwise; older lessons are being brought in line as they are reviewed.
writing.education: Education, not recommendations. We explain how things work and the trade-offs involved. We do not tell you what to do with your own money.

sources.heading: How we source facts
sources.intro: Where a lesson relies on a figure, rule or threshold, we cite a primary or official source in a Sources section on the page. We are moving every lesson to official UK sources such as:
sources.fca: the UK financial regulator, and its register of authorised firms
sources.ons: official statistics such as inflation and earnings
sources.outro: Other sources, such as reputable news or research, are used for context and are named when we rely on them.

updates.heading: Review dates and updates
updates.body: Each lesson and guide shows the date it was last reviewed or updated. When UK rules or thresholds change, for example at the start of a new tax year, we update the affected pages and the date changes with them.

corrections.heading: Corrections
corrections.body: If you spot a mistake or something out of date, tell us through our support page. We check every report, fix factual errors as quickly as we can and update the page's review date.

advice.heading: Not financial advice
advice.body: Garzoni is an education app, not a regulated financial adviser. Our lessons, guides, tools and AI coach give general information, not personal advice based on your circumstances.
advice.help: For advice about your own situation, consider a regulated financial adviser (you can check one on the FCA register) or free, impartial guidance from MoneyHelper.

about.seoTitle: About Garzoni — Financial Education for Young Adults
about.seoDescription: Garzoni is a personal finance education app that teaches budgeting, saving, investing and debt through short interactive lessons. Meet the founder and see how we write our lessons.
about.title: About Garzoni
about.intro: Garzoni is a personal finance education platform built for young adults who were never taught how money works. We turn budgeting, saving, investing, credit, debt and taxes into short, practical lessons you can finish in ten minutes.
about.missionBody: Financial literacy is one of the most useful skills a person can learn, yet most people leave school without it. Garzoni exists to close that gap and make financial education engaging, accessible and genuinely useful, not intimidating.
about.founderBody: Garzoni was founded by Andrei Neagoe, who writes and edits its lessons and guides. He holds a BSc in Computer Science from Queen Mary University of London.
about.founderDisclaimer: Garzoni is an education app, not a regulated financial adviser.
about.standardsBody: Lessons use plain language and UK context, cite official sources such as MoneyHelper, the FCA, HMRC and the Bank of England where a figure or rule matters, and show the date they were last reviewed.

how.lessonsBody: Bite-sized, jargon-free lessons that fit into a busy day.
how.repetitionBody: Knowledge checks resurface concepts over time so what you learn actually sticks.
how.coachBody: Garzoni's AI coach reads your inputs in the budget, debt and savings simulators and explains what changes and why, in plain language.
how.streaksBody: Daily streaks and experience points help you build the habit.

about.learnBody: Garzoni covers the core pillars of personal finance: building a budget, growing savings and an emergency fund, paying down debt, understanding credit scores, the basics of investing and navigating taxes, all grounded in real-world scenarios.
about.ctaBody: Create a free account to unlock the full learning path, quizzes, streaks and Garzoni's AI financial coach.

faq.whatA: Garzoni is a personal finance education app for young adults. It teaches budgeting, saving, investing, debt management, credit scores and taxes through interactive ten-minute lessons, daily streaks and an AI-powered financial coach.
faq.differentQ: How is Garzoni different from a budgeting app?
faq.differentA: Most finance apps track your money. Garzoni teaches you how money works. It is a learning platform, like Duolingo for personal finance, that builds lasting financial literacy through spaced repetition and hands-on simulators.
faq.whoA: Garzoni's lessons and guides are written and edited by its founder, Andrei Neagoe, following published editorial standards that favour official UK sources such as MoneyHelper, the FCA and HMRC.
faq.adviceA: No. Garzoni is a financial education app. It explains concepts and runs simulations, but it does not give personal recommendations and is not a regulated financial adviser.
